page: UpCloud PREMIUM-48xCPU-96GB is a KVM-hypervised virtual server featuring 48 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The system is equipped with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled as a 400 GB local SSD, and the configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Notably, the CPU allocation is designated as shared, which represents a potential performance tradeoff for sustained multi-core workloads despite the high physical core count.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in several compute-intensive areas. The server achieves top 10% placement in stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU evaluations, as well as in Geekbench single-core and multi-core scores. Software compilation with Clang, image processing, and text processing also register in the top 10% tier. Cryptographic and compression tasks perform strongly, with bzip3 decompression and gzip compression reaching top-tier throughput. Memory performance is more moderate, with Passmark memory scores falling in the middle 50% average tier, though uncached read memory bandwidth remains strong at 261.26 GB/sec.

Given the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server is structured for compute-heavy operations. The qualitative cost efficiency is characterized by high compute density relative to memory capacity, making it suitable for parallelizable tasks that do not require massive memory footprints. Appropriate workloads include software compilation, web serving, text and image processing, and moderate database operations. However, the shared CPU allocation suggests it is less optimal for continuous, non-burstable maximum-load high-performance computing compared to dedicated-core alternatives.
